messages:
maria: Heads-up — found a build artifact uploaded to a public CI artifacts bucket that contains what looks like a KMS-wrapped blob that decodes to a service account token. immediate triage please. :rotating_light:

aj: Oof. Can you paste the artifact path and a short snippet (no secrets) so we can confirm pattern?

maria: s3://ci-artifacts/redwood/build-2026-03-20/logs.tar.gz. snippet: `-----BEGIN KMS-WRAP-----A3f...==-----END KMS-WRAP-----` (removed body).

devon: confirmed pattern matches our KMS envelope format. That blob likely contains a JWT or kubernetes serviceaccount token that was wrapped using our KMS key for transit.

samir: Immediate actions I suggest: 1) mark artifact private / take down, 2) revoke that SA, 3) revoke any active kubeconfig that used it, 4) rotate KMS key or create new key version. I'll start with takedown.

maria: taken down (removed public-read, bucket ACL fixed). pulled local copy for analysis to a locked host.

aj: Revoke service account tokens: `kubectl delete secret -n infra deploy-sa-token-abc123` and remove any bound tokens. Also create a temporary RBAC rule to deny deploys from CI SA until we have root cause.

devon: Adding deny rule now: `kubectl create rolebinding deny-ci-impersonation --clusterrole=view --user=system:serviceaccount:ci:builder-sa --namespace=default --dry-run=client -o yaml | kubectl apply -f -` — actually that is not a deny. We'll patch the OPA gate to explicitly block impersonation for builder-sa.

elaine: Audit query: search for `BEGIN KMS-WRAP` across buckets and logs (S3, GCS) and CI job artifacts from last 30 days. I kicked off a lambda that scans objects and tags any match for review.

samir: On KMS rotation: rotating key is safest but expensive. Alternative: disable key versions for decryption for the current key, then create a new key and rewrap needed secrets. We should also check KMS key grants (who can decrypt).

maria: sec-bot flagged the artifact creation job: `ci/publish-logs` ran with elevated volume mounts and accidentally packaged `/var/run/secrets/k8s.io/serviceaccount`. There's a step that tarred the node filesystem.

aj: Root cause then: CI runner config. Fix: update job container to mount only workspace, not host /var/run. Add sanitization step: `find . -type f -name "*token*" -delete` before archive. Add test that job artifacts cannot contain PEM/JWT patterns.

devon: For immediate privilege reduction: I created a temporary clusterRoleBinding removal: `kubectl delete clusterrolebinding ci-builder-admin-binding` and locked the builder-sa to namespace-scoped roles only.

elaine: Audit log search results: found 2 other artifacts with same pattern in last 14 days, both from the same runner pool. Marked them for rotation and review.

maria: We need to rotate any credentials that could have been minted with that SA. List of owners: platform-team (devon), infra-cicd (aj), security (maria). Oncall — please run a live sweep for unusual API calls by that SA in the past 48h.

oncall: Running query now: `kubectl get events --all-namespaces --field-selector involvedObject.kind=Pod -o json | jq '.items[] | select(.source.user == "system:serviceaccount:ci:builder-sa")'` — no obvious mass deletes but there were a few deploys to dev cluster.

samir: Post-incident steps (short): 1) CI runner config hardening (no host mounts), 2) artifact scanner in CI before upload, 3) blocklist pattern detection for KMS envelopes, 4) automated SA token revocation playbook, 5) limit decrypt grants on KMS key to minimum set + require IAM condition.

aj: I'll open follow-up tickets: `SEC-1583` (CI runner mount lockdown), `SEC-1584` (artifact sanitizer), `SEC-1585` (KMS grant review). Assigning now.

devon: Also recommend enabling the admission controller change that prevents creation of secrets with names matching `*-token-*` in prod namespaces unless explicitly approved.

maria: For the interim, rotating the KMS key: `gcloud kms keys versions destroy --key my-key --location global --keyring redwood-keys --version 1` (we'll follow cloud provider best practices). We document the rotation steps in the incident playbook.

elaine: We'll need to run an eval to ensure no production workloads rely on decrypting old key versions unexpectedly. Plan a staged key rotation with a canary namespace.

samir: One more: update our least-priv checklist in PR reviews — require explicit statement for any CI job that mounts host paths.

maria: Good work team. Summarizing next steps: takedown (done), revoke SA tokens & remove clusterrolebinding (done), KMS grant review + rotation (in progress), artifact scan (in progress), CI job fixes + tests (todo). I'll schedule a postmortem tomorrow 10:00 PST.

aj: I'll attach the list of affected artifacts and the new CI job patch in SEC-1583. :thumbsup:

oncall: If anyone finds suspicious activity tied to builder-sa, ping #incidents and escalate.

sec-bot: Automated note: incident ticket created SEC-1582. Incident severity: P2.

maria: Thanks — closing the slack thread for live updates in the incident ticket.
